A philosopher, mystic and critic from Kashmir who lived from about 950 to about 1016. He is the great systematiser of Kashmir Shaivism and the most influential thinker in Indian aesthetics.

He came from a learned Brahmin family and studied with many teachers. His huge Tantraloka sets out the Trika school of Shaivism: the world is the free self-expression of one consciousness, Shiva, and liberation means recognising that one's own self is that consciousness.

His commentaries on the Natyashastra, the old manual of drama, and on Anandavardhana's theory of suggestion in poetry made him the authority on rasa, the "taste" or emotion an audience savours in art. He argued that rasa is a kind of calm, impersonal delight, close to spiritual insight, and defended a ninth rasa, peace. Indian critics of music, dance and poetry still work in his terms.

Kashmir later produced the poet Lal Ded, whose verses carry his school's ideas into the language of ordinary people.
sum: A philosopher, mystic and critic from Kashmir who lived from about 950 to about 1016. He is the great systematiser of Kashmir Shaivism and the most influential thinker in Indian aesthetics.
